# Evaluator Rubric

The checker in a maker-checker loop should judge every maker output against
this rubric, not its own ad hoc judgment -- the whole point of maker-checker
is that the check is repeatable and does not silently drift between
iterations.

## Pass criteria

- Every verification command declared in `harness.config.json` that applies
  to this change exits 0, and `verify --run` was actually invoked to prove
  it (not just claimed in prose).
- `node --test` (no path argument, no directory, no glob) shows the same
  pass count as before the change plus any tests the change itself added --
  never fewer. `node --check scripts/action.mjs scripts/assess.mjs
  scripts/diff.mjs scripts/scaffold.mjs scripts/verify.mjs` exits 0.
- If the change touches `references/rubric.md`, `references/failure-modes.md`,
  or any gap id / level gate / safety rule, `tests/docs.test.mjs` and
  `tests/rubric.test.mjs` still pass -- those are this repository's own
  doc-drift guards and a change that breaks them is not done regardless of
  what else passes.
- If the change targets a specific `assess` gap (a goal loop, see
  `loop/goal-loop.md`), that gap id no longer appears in
  `node scripts/assess.mjs .`'s output, and no gap that was previously
  absent has newly appeared as a side effect.

## Fail criteria

- Any declared verification command fails, or was never actually run.
- A change claims to be done without exit-code evidence to back it up.
- The change modifies `scripts/`, `templates/`, `skills/`, `references/`,
  `README*`, or `ROADMAP*` without the maker explicitly flagging that as an
  intentional, in-scope part of the task -- these are this project's own
  product surface, not incidental config, and an unflagged edit to any of
  them is treated as a scope violation regardless of whether it "improves"
  something.
- The change adds a runtime dependency, uses CommonJS `require` in a
  `scripts/**/*.mjs` file, or relies on a Node API not available on
  Node 20 -- all three break this project's own hard constraints
  (zero dependencies, ESM, `>=20`) even if every test still passes.

On a fail, the loop should route back to the maker with the specific
failure, not a vague "try again" -- see `loop/maker-checker-loop.md` for how
the two roles hand off.
